youtube_title: In Texas, Bees Can Change a Landowner's Property Tax Bill 🦝⚖️
caption: Texas allows agricultural (productivity) appraisal of qualifying land, and its tax code counts beekeeping on 5 to 20 acres as agricultural use — subject to local intensity standards, history requirements and documentation.
script: In Texas, keeping bees on your land can legally slash your property taxes. [disclaimer] Bees! Seriously! Here's how it works. Texas lets farm land be taxed based on what it can produce, instead of what it would sell for. And the state says that number is usually way lower. To qualify, the land usually has to be used mainly for farming, at the level that's normal in that area. And it has to have been farmed for at least five of the last seven years. Now here's the bee part. Texas changed its tax law to say that keeping bees counts as farming! Land used to raise bees, for pollination or for stuff like honey, can qualify. But only if the land is at least five acres and no more than twenty. So picture this. Someone owns ten acres and starts keeping bees on it. If it really meets all the rules, the land's tax value could drop toward the farm value. Buzz buzz, tax break! But it's not an instant trick. Local tax offices set their own rules, like how many hives you need per acre. And your house itself doesn't disappear from the tax bill. This is only about the land being used for farming.
